questions.question: Compare the properties of clay before and after firing.
questions.expected_answer: Before firing, clay is soft, sticky and easy to shape, and dried clay turns soft again in water. After firing, it is very hard and strong, rings a little when tapped and does not soften in water.

questions.question: Describe how you would test whether a new material is hard, strong and waterproof.
questions.expected_answer: For hardness, try to scratch it with a steel nail. For strength, put it on a table and add weights on top until it cracks. For waterproofness, drip water onto it and watch for a minute to see whether the water soaks in.

questions.question: Give one example of a change that can be undone and one that cannot. Why is it useful that some changes cannot be undone?
questions.expected_answer: Jelly melting and setting again, or ice melting and freezing, can be undone. Baking bread, firing clay or setting concrete cannot be undone. It is useful because the new materials keep their new properties, so bricks stay hard in the rain and bridges do not turn back into sand.
